subject: general
question: Jaggu can make one wooden chair in 3 days and Rabbu can make the same chair in 4 days. If they work together, in how many days will they make 14 chairs of the same kind?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rate of **Jaggu** = 1/3 chairs/day and Rate of **Rabbu** = 1/4 chairs/day.

Combined rate = (1/3 + 1/4) = 7/12 chairs/day.

Number of days for 14 chairs = Total chairs ÷ Combined rate.

Required days = 14 ÷ (7/12) = 14 × (12/7) = 2 × 12 = 24 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 24 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by **Jaggu** for 1 chair = 3 days.

Time taken by **Rabbu** for 1 chair = 4 days.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

⇒ Combined efficiency of **Jaggu** and **Rabbu** = 4 + 3 = 7 units/day.

⇒ Units of work required to make 1 chair = 12 units.

⇒ Total work for **14 chairs** = 14 × 12 = 168 units.

⇒ Days required = Total units ÷ Combined efficiency

⇒ Days required = 168 ÷ 7 = 24 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 24 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Combined Efficiency Rule

When two or more people work together, their individual rates of work (efficiencies) are added to determine the collective rate of progress.

Work and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time. If A can do a work in x days, his efficiency is 1/x of the work per day.

Total Work Assumption

Assuming Total Work as the LCM of individual days simplifies calculations by avoiding fractions in efficiency values.</p
